findings.reason: Glob shows the only .ts files are decimal.d.ts and decimal.global.d.ts, so nothing compiles the typings or checks narrowing; the isDecimal tests at test/modules/isFiniteEtc.js:261-277 are runtime JS and pass either way. The guard itself is sound, since isDecimalInstance (decimal.js:4534) is the runtime check. This is a test-coverage gap in a repo that has never type-tested, not a defect, so it stays low.
findings.claim: The new type-guard signature for isDecimal has no type-level test (compile or narrowing check), so a later regression in the typings would go unnoticed.
findings.evidence: The diff only changes `static isDecimal(object: any): boolean` to `static isDecimal(object: any): object is Decimal;` in decimal.d.ts:254 and decimal.global.d.ts:275. No .ts test file exists in the repo; the only isDecimal tests are runtime JS assertions in test/modules/isFiniteEtc.js:261-277, which pass with or without this change. The guard is sound against the runtime: isDecimalInstance (decimal.js:4534) returns `obj instanceof Decimal || obj && obj.toStringTag === tag || false`.
